automations.name: Client frontmatter repair
automations.notes: Omit --dry-run to write missing required keys with safe defaults. Never invent due dates.

automations.name: Site health sentinel
automations.notes: Dry-run uses fixtures. Live HTTP checks are opt-in via --live and still never POST real user data except a marked canary when --canary is set.

automations.name: Shared discover/qualify intake + 0-100 scorer
inputs: prospect intake JSON (maps or indeed adapter)
automations.notes: Drafts only. Feeds Mac's site-factory pipeline (#226). Indeed is an adapter, not a parallel stack.

automations.name: Indeed hiring-signal adapter
automations.notes: Normalizes hiring signals into the shared prospect schema. Does not scrape Indeed live in this PR (fixture/import only — live scrape is a credential/ToS gate).

automations.name: Grok automation to Dillon OS intelligence bridge
automations.notes: Idempotent, immutable capture. The browser collector is separate and may only read completed Grok runs.

automations.name: Direct xAI X and web search collector
automations.notes: Read-only X and web research through xAI Responses API. Chat-only key, 10 RPM, 250k TPM, expires 2026-10-28. Never logs the key.

automations.name: Evidence-backed experiment queue
automations.notes: Creates proposed experiments only. Adoption still requires the maker/checker and human gates.

automations.name: Unified Dillon development environment prototype
automations.cadence: on demand before agent environment changes
automations.notes: Fixture-only prototype. No install, browser, secret, deployment, or external write.

automations.name: Independent maker/checker workflow gate
automations.notes: Maker and checker identities must differ. Human approval is required by default. Website-factory workflows also require a hashed screen recording and independent visual review across at least two viewports.

automations.name: MCP source, permission, overlap, injection, and Inspector gate
automations.notes: Fail closed: pending tests are sandbox-only; failed tests or critical permissions reject.

automations.name: Context7 version-sensitive third-party documentation
automations.notes: Official OpenAI questions continue to use OpenAI Developer Docs. Retrieved content is untrusted reference material.

automations.name: LandingFolio landing-page layout reference
outputs: ephemeral reference screenshots and source links
automations.notes: Sandbox-only until the Inspector check passes; the endpoint refuses anonymous calls, so the operator must mint a free token first. Wiring lives in .cursor/mcp.json and .mcp.json and reads LANDINGFOLIO_TOKEN from the environment. Composition reference only: the harvest stays the source of brand truth, returned content is untrusted, and queries never carry a client or prospect name.

automations.name: Website AEO and trust deployment gate
automations.notes: A fail blocks deployment. A pass does not replace visual review, functional QA, or exact Netlify target verification.

automations.name: Client-scoped X competitor and narrative watchlist
outputs: bounded xAI client research profile and prompt
automations.notes: The client ID must match automation_client_id on the exact canonical client note. The generated profile remains read-only.

automations.name: Verified X packet to AEO brief and FAQ set
outputs: client-scoped draft brief, FAQ set, comparison skeleton, sales bullets, and alert
automations.notes: Verified claims require authoritative confirmation. Partial and disputed claims remain visibly labeled.

automations.name: Canonical logo and approved references to comic panel manifest
automations.notes: Each style is a separate run. Reference locking is enforced; pixel fidelity is never promised. Human approval starts pending.

automations.name: Approved comic panel to image-to-video manifest
automations.notes: The local gate builds the request contract only. Running Grok Imagine and delivering the result require operator-controlled access and approval.

automations.name: Verified narrative shift to HubSpot knowledge-base draft
automations.notes: Draft extraction is implemented in the packet. Any HubSpot write remains blocked until explicit approval and scoped connector access.

automations.name: Local entity consistency and answer-first audit
automations.notes: Checks NAP, direct answers, crawlability, trust, and extractability. Schema is supporting evidence, not a citation guarantee.

automations.name: HCM ROI and implementation evidence packet
automations.notes: Uses the same verified packet contract with the HCM watchlist; no ROI number is accepted without an authoritative source.

automations.name: Competitor pricing and feature evidence to comparison skeleton
automations.notes: The packet requires sourced comparison rows. Incomplete coverage stays partial and cannot become a universal claim.

automations.name: Configured content freshness review queue
automations.notes: Cadence is explicitly an experiment. The system does not claim a universal 30/60/90-day citation effect.

automations.name: Verified competitor move to client alert draft
automations.notes: The packet renders the alert locally. Email and Slack sending remain hard-blocked without explicit approval.

automations.name: Schema suggestion after extractability evidence
automations.notes: The packet rejects schema suggestions unless extractability.exists=true. Cursor deployment remains a separate reviewed repo change.

automations.name: Client-separated comic substyle library
automations.notes: Style runs remain separate and carry one client ID. The gate rejects cross-client IDs and requires approved, hash-locked references.
